variables.name: nNode
variables.meaning: portable content nodes visited while constructing one document index

variables.name: kID
variables.meaning: ID-bearing content nodes retained by the index

variables.name: dDepth
variables.meaning: maximum document nesting depth represented by the explicit traversal stack

assumptions: Core Tree construction is linear in retained ID-bearing nodes
deterministicWork: each accepted content node is pushed/visited at most once by the explicit stack
each ID-bearing node contributes one node/location/tree-input entry
contract.resourceRationale: DocumentIndex retains one node and location entry per ID-bearing node plus the Core Tree view; anonymous text and hard-break nodes are visited but not retained.
contract.proof: The iterative traversal consumes each bounded child sequence once, records each ID-bearing node once, and passes exactly those retained IDs to Core Tree construction.
contract.adversarialWitness: The 50k-root-paragraph resource proof and resource-ceiling tests exercise broad and deep documents without recursive Content traversal.

fullScan.rationale: Explicit index construction must observe the full accepted document once.

variables.name: lText
variables.meaning: code units copied for the edited canonical text surface and replacement

variables.name: wPath
variables.meaning: sum of changed ancestor child-array widths copied while rebuilding the persistent document path

variables.name: tOverride
variables.meaning: prior changed ID-bearing node overrides copied into the next prepared state

variables.name: kID
variables.meaning: ID-bearing nodes retained by the prepared base index

assumptions: prepared state was validated and indexed before the local edit
this fast path accepts only an empty surface or one canonical text run
ceilings: text and ancestor work remain within Content resource ceilings
unsupported inline structure is rejected instead of falling back to hidden global work
deterministicWork: target lookup reuses retained DocumentIndex state
only the changed node and its ancestor path are rebuilt
the proof performs no whole-document validation/index reconstruction after preparation
contract.resourceRationale: The prepared state retains one base index plus changed-node overrides; each edit shares unchanged nodes and rebuilds only the changed structural path, while current array-backed containers copy their changed child array.
contract.proof: replacePreparedText resolves the target from the retained index, copies text once, reconstructs the indexed ancestor path, overlays changed node identities, and returns the next prepared state without calling full validation or createDocumentIndex.
contract.adversarialWitness: At 50k root paragraphs the prepared proof measures about 0.16–0.20 ms for one local edit after preparation and about 0.18 ms/edit across 1,000 distinct edited nodes, while the semantic whole-clone proof is about 190–220 ms for one local edit.

fullScan.rationale: Prepared local edits must not scan or rebuild the full validated document; copying the explicitly changed container array is a documented width cost.
